title: OpenXR: ignore important return values.
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in master (4.5 beta1, 46c495ca21f40f57a7fb9c7cde6143738f1652d4)

### System information

Any OpenXR capable system (tested on Windows 11, Quest over steam link)

### Issue description

This is something we ran into by accident and just never implemented properly.

OpenXR defines 3 outcomes of any OpenXR API call:
- A return value of `XR_SUCCESS (0)`, which means the call did what it was supposed to do
- A negative return value, which means the call failed
- A positive return value, which means something non-critical prevented or limited execution.

Almost everywhere we use the `XR_FAILED` macro which check any negative return value, and error out in that situation.
This means that positive return values get ignored which in 99% of the cases is the correct behaviour.

But in 1% it may not lead to problems, but it does result in us missing something important.

The suggestion is to work our way through our OpenXR implementation and change our error handling so we at the very least report positive return values as warnings or verbose output.

### Steps to reproduce

Currently this can be best reproduced by checking the output of `xrSyncActions` while the user is NOT wearing their headset, either with a breakpoint or by logging the output when non-zero.

When the session is anything other than focused, the return value will be `XR_SESSION_NOT_FOCUSED`.

We are only supposed to call `xrSyncActions` when the user is wearing the headset and there isn't another reason we're not in the focused state. We will be fixing that particular issue separate from this issue as there is a larger impact than simply calling `xrSyncActions` too often.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

This can be tested with any OpenXR project in https://github.com/godotengine/godot-demo-projects/tree/master/xr
